anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are adequate.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Free physical or logical space for data, logs, or temporary areas reaches exhaustion limits.
CPU Resource Anomaly: Database processes drive the host CPU close to saturation, leaving too few cycles for the rest of the workload.

When all three root causes are present, the database exhibits a cascade of intertwined symptoms: a plan regression suddenly switches selective index access to full scans or hash joins that spill to disk, inflating both CPU consumption and temporary-space usage. Temp segments and growing undo or redo logs fill remaining storage, triggering allocation failures, auto-extend stalls, log-archive back-pressure, and "out of space" errors. At the same time, the CPU remains pegged, lengthening every I/O request, catalog access, and background maintenance task, so space-reclamation jobs, log shipping, and plan-cache management all slow down. The result is erratic but severe query latency, widespread enqueue and scheduler waits, repeated plan recompilations due to cache eviction, and sudden session aborts when space or CPU limits are finally breached.

Causally, a poor plan initiates excessive buffer touches, parallel threads, and large intermediate result sets, directly driving CPU load and temp-space consumption. Elevated CPU utilization delays checkpoint, archive, and cleanup processes, preventing timely space recycling. As storage fills, the optimizer may abandon previously viable plans that require work areas or create new plans that favor CPU-heavy in-memory operations, further worsening CPU saturation. Space exhaustion can also invalidate or flush plans, forcing more compilations and again increasing CPU pressure. This feedback loop between bad plans, CPU saturation, and space shortages rapidly degrades overall database stability and makes single-factor remediation ineffective until all three dimensions are addressed together.

entry.official_definition: The execution timeout for SELECT statements, in milliseconds.
entry.trigger_condition: A SELECT statement exceeds the configured max_execution_time limit.
entry.workload_impact: The SELECT statement is interrupted by the execution time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
